status: registered before execution; G-T4 learned interpolator vs linear baseline
question: Does a small learned, continuous-time interpolator predict the OlmoEarth single-observation embedding at a held-out date better than date-weighted linear interpolation of its two neighbours, on regions never seen in training?
data: olmo_streaming_dev/single_fp16 (12 single-observation embeddings per tile, 768x32x32), real dates from contract (12-of-15 sealed selection). Synthetic-month encoding caveat carried from MS-126.

split.test_rule: the three regions with the lowest linear-baseline cos in MS-126; fixed before training

models.resmlp: per-token MLP on [S_prev, S_next, linear, w, gap/365, sin/cos doy_target] predicting a residual added to linear (768*3+4 -> 512 -> 768)
models.ctxattn: per-token 2-layer transformer (d=256, 4 heads) over the 11 context observations, each with continuous time encoding (sin/cos doy, signed dt to target / 365); query token = target time; output 768

objective: MSE + (1 - cos) on the target single embedding; interior slots j=1..10; tokens subsampled 128 per tile per step
training: AdamW 1e-3 wd 1e-4, cosine, 20000 steps, batch 8 tiles x 128 tokens, 3 seeds per model, GPU1
metrics: mean token cos on test regions, all interior slots and all tokens; by gap bin as in MS-126; bootstrap CI over tiles (2000 resamples)

decision_rules.G-T4_pass: best learned model beats linear by >= +0.03 mean cos on test regions with the 95% bootstrap CI of the paired difference excluding 0, for at least 2 of 3 seeds
decision_rules.G-T4_fail: otherwise: method claim withdrawn; benchmark (MS-126) and MS-125 curve remain
decision_rules.secondary: gain must not come only from gap<=40d; report gap>120d separately
